keyword: how long is the artemis 2 mission

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission is scheduled to last approximately 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "10-day mission" (R1, R3); "10-day mission" (R2); "approximately 10 days" (R4); "10-day mission" (R5); "10 days — or, rather, a little short of 10 days" (R6); "nearly 10 days" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the mission lasts approximately 10 days.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission will take four astronauts around the Moon and back.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "four astronauts toward space... around the moon but not land there" (R1); "four astronauts... orbit the Moon" (R2); "four astronauts on board the Orion spacecraft" around Moon (R3, R5, R6, R7)
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm four specific astronauts on a mission around the Moon and back without landing.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission includes orbital checks.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "check important systems aboard Orion, including life support... in a high-Earth orbit" (R1); "series of systems checks" after orbit (R5); "check out Orion systems, including life support systems" in Earth orbit (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe systems checks in Earth orbit before translunar injection, but not precisely termed 'orbital checks'; broader support.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission includes a lunar flyby.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "swing around, passing over the far side" (R1); "lunar flyby" (R5, R7); "flight around the moon" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly describe a lunar flyby or equivalent trajectory around the Moon's far side.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission includes a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splashdown in the Pacific Ocean" (R1); "splashdown... in the Pacific Ocean, off the coast of San Francisco" (R5); "splashdown off the coast of San Diego" (R6, R7)
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources confirm splashdown in the Pacific Ocean.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission is a test flight verifying the Orion spacecraft's life-support systems with a crew on board.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "check that the spacecraft can safely... keep its crew alive" (R1); "verify modern human capabilities in deep space" (R2); "check out Orion systems, including life support systems" with crew (R6); "testing all of its life-support... with a crew of four on board" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe it as a crewed test verifying life-support and other systems.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission is expected to conclude on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splashdown in the Pacific Ocean on April 10"; launch context April 1, 2026 (URL: 2026/04/01)
verifications.reasoning: R1 directly states splashdown on April 10 following April 1, 2026 launch; other sources confirm ~10-day duration aligning with this date.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission duration is nine days, one hour, and 46 minutes.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splashdown will take place nine days, one hour and 46 minutes after liftoff"
verifications.reasoning: R6 provides the exact duration matching the claim.

verifications.claim: The astronauts of the Artemis 2 mission will not land on the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "around the moon but not land there" (R1); "will not land on the moon (that will happen on Artemis IV)" (R4); no landing mentioned, flyby only (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state no landing on the Moon.

verifications.claim: The astronauts of the Artemis 2 mission will orbit the Moon.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: "orbit the Moon" (R2, loose); "eschews Orion's entry into lunar orbit" (R5); free-return trajectory around the moon, no orbit (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Most sources describe a flyby/free-return trajectory without entering lunar orbit; R2 uses 'orbit' loosely, but precise sources contradict.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission marks the first human lunar flyby in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "first time since 1972"; "more than 50 years" (R1, R2, R3); "first human lunar flyby in more than half a century" (R5); "first... in more than 50 years" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently state it is the first crewed lunar mission/flyby since Apollo 17 in 1972, over 50 years.
